facts: **Area $=\dfrac{h(a+b)}{2}$**, where $a$ and $b$ are the two **parallel** sides and $h$ is the perpendicular height.
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides, shown by the arrow marks in a figure.
The height $h$ is the **perpendicular** distance between the parallel sides, never a slanting side.
In a right-angled trapezium the side drawn at a right angle to both parallel sides **is** the height.
All three lengths must be in the same unit, and the area is written in square units: mm$^{2}$, cm$^{2}$, m$^{2}$.
steps: Identify the two parallel sides $a$ and $b$ and the perpendicular height $h$.
Add the parallel sides, multiply by $h$, halve, and write the answer with squared units.

development.question_text: The parallel sides of a trapezium are $9$ cm and $15$ cm long, and the perpendicular distance between them is $6$ cm. Find the area of the trapezium, in square centimetres.
A trapezium has parallel sides of $4.2$ m and $5.8$ m, and a perpendicular height of $3$ m. Find its area, in square metres.

mastery.solution_text:
The parallel sides are the two vertical sides, $7$ cm and $3$ cm, and the $3$ cm side joins them at right angles, so it is the height.
$A=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}$
$=\frac{3(7+3)}{2}$
$=\frac{3 \times 10}{2}$
$=\frac{30}{2}$
$=15\text{ cm}^2$

mastery.question_text:
Trapezium P and trapezium Q both have a perpendicular height of $6$ cm. Trapezium P has parallel sides $5$ cm and $11$ cm; trapezium Q has parallel sides $7$ cm and $9$ cm.
Show that the two trapeziums have equal areas, in square centimetres.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{\text{P}}=\frac{6(5+11)}{2}$
$=\frac{6 \times 16}{2}$
$=48\text{ cm}^2$
$A_{\text{Q}}=\frac{6(7+9)}{2}$
$=\frac{6 \times 16}{2}$
$=48\text{ cm}^2$
The parallel sides add to $16$ cm in both trapeziums, so both areas are $48$ cm$^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: The two parallel sides of a trapezium differ in length by $4$ cm. The shorter parallel side is $6$ cm and the perpendicular height is $5$ cm. Find the area of the trapezium, in square centimetres.
